newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela judge bans single-hull tankers - paper.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela judge bans single-hull tankers - paper.

text.p: A regional Venezuelan judge banned single-hulled oil tankers from using Lake Maracaibo shipping channel following a 25,000 barrel oil spill on February 28, Venezuela's El Nacional newspaper reported on Tuesday.
Judge Ricardo Colmenares in the eastern city of Cabimas ruled that the ban would become effective on April 16 and enforcement would be carried out by the Navy, the newspaper reported.
Reuters was not able to confirm the story immediately.

"Colmenares communicated with the presidency of Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) and its subsidiaries, with the intention of notifying them of the ban on chartering or selling oil (and oil products) on single-hulled vessels which use Maracaibo Lake shipping channel," El Nacional reported.
On February 28, the single-hulled Nissos Amorgos tanker ran aground as it passed through the channel, spilling about 25,000 barrels of heavy crude.
El Nacional said Colmenares noted that double-hulls are required by international agreements to prevent marine pollution, specifically MARPOL 73-78.
